1c11e74b-d59a-4ac4-a848-46969bc88966.description: Error ratio over 5m is above 14.4x the 1% error budget (fast burn); at this rate a 30-day budget lasts about 2 days.

facts.statement: Checkout is the only service with a high error ratio (0.45). Frontend is at 0.024 and frontend-proxy at 0.023.
Checkout revision 2 was created at 19:25:01Z with the change cause 'payment client moved to port 9999'. Revision 1 was created at 19:12:15Z.
The diff between revisions 1 and 2 changes containers.checkout.env.PAYMENT_ADDR from payment:8080 to payment:9999.
Checkout's error spans are PaymentService/Charge and PlaceOrder failing with 'connection error ... dial tcp 10.96.155.32:9999: i/o timeout'. Frontend's POST /api/checkout returns 500 as a result.
Payment's logs contain only info lines (Charge request received, Transaction complete). They stop at 19:24:57Z, with no error lines.
Payment's Charge server-span rate falls from about 0.2 per second to 0 between 19:20Z and 19:28Z.
Checkout's client Charge call rate is 0.217 per second over 5m. Checkout's own error logs are empty.
Checkout's error ratio climbs from 0.275 at 19:26 to 0.590 at 19:27:54Z.
All 18 flags are off. Warning events show only probe failures on otel-collector, alertmanager and loki, not on checkout or payment.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check the payment Service ports and the payment container's listening port. Then confirm a connect to payment:9999 is refused or times out.
hypotheses.statement: Payment's Kubernetes Service and container listen on 8080 only, so nothing listens on 9999.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Run kubectl rollout undo for checkout, then watch service:sli_error_ratio:rate5m for checkout drop toward zero.
hypotheses.statement: Rolling checkout back to revision 1 (PAYMENT_ADDR=payment:8080) should restore the error ratio to baseline.

inferences.statement: The port change at 19:25Z is the trigger. Payment is healthy on its own side and is not receiving checkout's charge calls, so the fault is in checkout's configuration.

root_causes.cause: Config release at 19:25Z set PAYMENT_ADDR to payment:9999, but payment serves on 8080. Every charge call from checkout times out, so PlaceOrder fails with Unavailable and about 45% of checkout requests return errors.

diagnosis.summary: Checkout's error ratio rose from about 0.28 to 0.59 over the last hour, peaking at 19:27Z. The checkout Deployment's revision 2 was rolled out at 19:25:01Z with the change cause 'payment client moved to port 9999'. The diff shows PAYMENT_ADDR changed from payment:8080 to payment:9999. Checkout's PaymentService/Charge calls fail with 'i/o timeout' dialing 10.96.155.32:9999, and payment's Charge server spans fall to zero after the rollout. Payment itself shows no errors, and no flags or warning events explain the change. Frontend and frontend-proxy errors are downstream of checkout.

actions.reason: Checkout revision 2 (19:25:01Z, 'payment client moved to port 9999') changed PAYMENT_ADDR from payment:8080 to payment:9999. Checkout's Charge calls fail with i/o timeout dialing port 9999, and payment's Charge spans fall to zero, so rolling back to revision 1 restores the working address.

alternatives.why_not: The fault is in the pod's environment configuration, not a stuck or leaking process. A restart would bring back the same PAYMENT_ADDR=payment:9999.
Checkout is not short of capacity. Its requests fail on a bad dial target, so more replicas would fail the same way.
Doing nothing leaves about 45% of checkout requests failing and the fast error budget burn running.

plan.summary: Roll checkout back to revision 1, which restores PAYMENT_ADDR=payment:8080 and undoes the 19:25Z release that pointed checkout at a port payment does not serve. Expect checkout's error ratio to fall from about 0.59 back to baseline (about 0.01) within a few minutes as charge calls succeed again.
